headline: The taper is holding after yesterday's sharp tempo — no follow-up run, which is the right call. Legs got their fast stimulus; now the quiet returns with under two weeks to the crossing.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: Running has done its job for this phase: the recent four-week block ran well ahead of the prior one, and yesterday's brisk tempo confirmed the aerobic engine still has a top end without dulling the legs. Today's absence of a run reads as deliberate spacing after that harder effort, not a gap. Strength has settled into a genuinely low-intensity, functional cadence — short sessions sitting mostly in the easiest zone — which is exactly what you want as departure nears, since it's maintenance, not a new stressor. Steps stay high on training days and drop sharply on rest days, so background time-on-feet remains substantial even when no run is logged. The strain-to-tolerance figure flagging "detraining" is an artefact of the winding-down volume against a fuller 28-day window — treat it as the taper showing up in the math, not a fitness warning. Recovery remains the one genuinely uneven input: sleep is erratic night to night.
sections.trends: The medium-term shape is a clear build into recent weeks followed by an intentional wind-down — cyclical rather than plateauing, and the timing lines up with the event on the horizon. Year-to-date volume dwarfs the same point last year, so this taper sits atop a far deeper base than the raw recent numbers alone suggest. That's the right frame: the quiet weeks are drawing down from a genuinely accumulated foundation, not from a thin one. For a hybrid athlete who maintains year-round readiness, this looks like a deliberate sharpening arc, not a loss of momentum.
sections.threshold: Threshold sits on a single early-July reference point with no 30-day baseline yet, so the number is a marker rather than a trend. What yesterday's tempo showed — sustained time above threshold at the quickest pace in weeks, with the effort held rather than surged — is the more useful current read: aerobic-threshold fitness is intact and accessible on demand. Nothing here suggests the top end has eroded during the lower-volume stretch.
sections.zones: The recent distribution is appropriate for a taper: most runs have lived low in the aerobic band with minimal grey-zone drift, and yesterday's session was the deliberate exception — a real chunk of time in the harder zones, cleanly polarised against the easy days around it rather than a muddy moderate slog. That's the right way to place a single quality effort inside a wind-down. Strength sessions sit almost entirely in the lowest zone, which keeps them as maintenance rather than competing for recovery.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength HR continues to sit low and controlled across sessions, consistent with functional maintenance work rather than anything metabolically taxing. The one run where the chest strap dropped out fell in line with surrounding efforts, so source agreement isn't raising any flags. Nothing notable to add beyond that.
sections.calendar: The pattern shows running and strength interleaved on a regular rhythm, with rest days that clearly correspond to the lowered step counts — you genuinely stop on stop days rather than backfilling with junk mileage. That discipline matters more now than at any point in the block: the ability to hold true rest through a taper is a skill, and the calendar shows it's in place.
sections.personal_bests: No PBs are in realistic reach right now, nor should they be — the shorter-distance bests date from a faster-focused window last autumn, and current training is pointed at multi-day loaded durability, a different quality entirely. The tempo confirms the speed hasn't vanished, but chasing a PB now would work against the taper. Park it for after the crossing.

watch_items: Watch whether any residual soreness or heaviness from the tempo lingers a second day, since that would matter more this close to departure than in a normal week.
Watch that the next runs drop back into the easy band rather than drifting toward yesterday's intensity as habit.
Watch how sleep tracks as travel and pre-event logistics ramp up — note it, don't chase it.
Watch that strength stays maintenance-level and short right through to departure rather than becoming a late durability substitute.
